title: Chapter 3: To You Who Are Surprisingly Close, and to You Who Feel Breathtakingly Far Away 1
content: Exiled Marquis Daughter's Adventurer Life
"Therefore, let's aim for the big game."
I discarded the question of what "therefore" meant.
Erika's eyes were saying, "Let's make some money."

The day after we defeated the Golden Ogre and used the money from selling its magic stone to upgrade Erika's equipment and my sword, while also donating the remaining funds entirely to the orphanage, it was early morning.
We were having breakfast at a diner for adventurers.
Erika jumped straight to the point, suggesting we aim for the big game, something a desperate adventurer in debt might say, and the reason was simple: money. We were out of it.
Even though Erika was once a marquis daughter, her father, the Prime Minister, couldn't openly provide assistance. However, when it came to money, he could surely arrange something.
Despite this, there was a reason Erika was talking about being in debt. Yesterday, after we returned home, all geared up and excited from hunting monsters, we were met by a man.
Though I stumbled during my first job with Erika, everything ended up settling down nicely. We had gathered our adventurer gear, and I was excited about the bright future ahead with Erika.
I never expected things would take such a sudden turn from that situation.
"I am not accustomed to making money, so I think it would be best to earn it through something I am familiar with," Erika declared confidently.
What could it mean that the best way for a former noble lady to earn money was through monster subjugation?
But it was true. Until recently, Erika had never had to earn money as a marquis daughter. If she was to do something she was most familiar with, it would indeed be adventuring.
"However, for a down payment on a house, a 'normal' big game won't suffice," I replied while breaking apart a fried chicken egg with my fork. I popped the soft yolk wrapped in ham into my mouth.
As I savored the egg and ham, I recalled the man from yesterday.
He seemed like an honest man.

As the sun began to set, he had been waiting for us in front of our house. With a truly apologetic demeanor and a firm resolve, he said, "I’m sorry, but I would like to collect the payment for the house."
Yes, that's right.
The payment for the house, our house.
It was more shocking than waking up to a dragon's breath, but it seemed we had failed to pay for our house. By the way, I thought he was a scam artist.
However, after talking with the man, I realized that we genuinely hadn't paid for the house.
To keep it brief, it turned out that the payment made by the Prime Minister, Erika's father, had not reached the man for some reason, as indicated by the contract presented.
The contract used for high-value transactions is a type of magic tool, so if it was unpaid, there was no choice but to believe it.

In cross-border transactions, the higher the amount, the more common it is to involve a reliable merchant to prevent payment delays. However, due to the circumstances, the Prime Minister had not involved a merchant this time.

That had backfired. The money that should have been paid by the Prime Minister was probably lying somewhere in a warehouse. According to a friend from my academy days, this kind of thing happens occasionally.
In most cases, it’s just an accident, and with time, it can be found.
But still.
"That said, I can't exactly ask him to wait."
That's right. Time was not on our side.

The good-natured man had already waited quite a while by the time he came to inform us of the unpaid amount. He had finally come to talk to us, thinking the sale of the house would be imminent. While it wasn't a matter of tomorrow or the day after, it seemed unlikely that I could inform the Prime Minister that the money hadn’t been paid and have him prepare it in time.
If that were the case, the man would have to find another buyer. I had asked him to wait, but the time granted was only two weeks.

Well, even getting two weeks was fortunate, considering he had no reason to consider our circumstances. He was a genuinely good man, as honest as he appeared, and I regretted thinking of him as a scam artist.

He mentioned that if we could pay a portion as a down payment, he could wait a little longer. However, that down payment was quite a significant amount. For the second son of a poor viscount, it felt like an unrealistically large sum, almost like a dream.
"From what I understand, adventurers can aim for a quick fortune, right?"
As I was about to groan over the unrealistic amount, Erika asked with a puzzled expression. Ah, I see. Erika was misunderstanding. Or rather, it was a difference in upbringing.
"Well, aiming for that amount immediately would be a bit difficult with a regular big game."
I shrugged and answered Erika's question.
"For a typical adventurer, the money from three Golden Ogres' magic stones would be enough to fall into the category of a quick fortune."

As expected of a former high noble, Erika's sense of money was different from that of a poor viscount's second son, or even a commoner. While she likely wouldn't treat that amount as pocket change, seeing her genuinely impressed by my words made me lose confidence.
"Then let's aim for an extraordinary big game."
Oh no, this is──.
Erika said with a smile that suggested she had come up with a good idea.
"It would be just right to raise your rank as an adventurer 'on the side' as well."
I realized cold sweat was running down my back as I drank from my wooden cup.

At first, I thought I was just overthinking it, but it seemed Erika was overestimating me. It’s not something to brag about, but I’m quite ordinary. I simply trained hard under a good mentor, and while I might have some confidence in body enhancement and healing magic compared to my peers, I was just a person who could swing a sword without being able to use magic.
As I was feeling exasperated by my ordinariness, Erika clapped her hands as if to say it was a good idea.
"Thinking about it that way, it’s just right. We can raise your adventurer rank 'on the side' while earning the down payment. It’s what you call killing two birds with one stone."
Impressive, but there was nothing that connected "just right" and "on the side."
The amount of the down payment that needed to be earned was one thing, but raising an adventurer rank couldn't simply be done "on the side."
For adventurers, a rank is merely a badge of honor, but for the Adventurer Guild, it’s not that simple. It’s proof of the adventurer's abilities certified by the guild.

We adventurers are foolish, so we perceive that up to rank 4, we are still within the realm of humans. From rank 5, we are half human, and from rank 7, we are no longer human at all. However, for the Adventurer Guild, that ranking is serious as it relates to the guild's credibility.
By the way, the highest rank of 10 is an honorary title given either to the head of the Adventurer Guild or to high-ranking adventurers who meet a heroic end, so no active adventurer desires it.
Additionally, graduates from the academy are generally considered to have the strength of ranks 4 to 5, indicating the academy's training capabilities are genuine.
Normally, commoner adventurers take years of time and risk their lives just to reach rank 3.
Ah, I’ve strayed far off topic. It’s a form of escapism.
In any case, there’s no way that a large down payment and an adventurer rank could be connected by "just right" and "on the side."
What do you think? Isn’t it a good idea?
The look on Erika's face as she gazed at me was one for the ages, but I couldn't nod in agreement so easily.
Moreover──.
"I'd prefer to avoid drawing too much attention."
I said while scratching my head.

Erika had been exiled as punishment for an attempted assassination of the Light Priestess. If the church that had once allowed her exile saw her standing out in her new location, it was uncertain how they would react. Furthermore, Erika's life was at stake. While the attack had only happened once, I couldn't be optimistic enough to think that would be the end of it.
To be honest, I would prefer to stay holed up at home until I figured out who was after Erika.
Well, currently, it seemed that home was about to disappear.
"Shin..."
Erika looked at me with an unusually questioning expression.
"Are you... not enthusiastic about this?"
About what, I wondered?
Was it about finding and killing the person who put you in this situation?
Or was it about earning the down payment for a house to live with Erika?

The answer was that I was motivated for both. I was confident that if I got the green light from Erika, I would charge ahead without hesitation. I had more confidence than a dog chasing a thrown stick.
However, I couldn’t just say that outright.
It would seem too desperate for someone who would only be playing a supporting role in this farce for about a year. Even I, a socially awkward person, could tell it would come off as a bit creepy.
For nobles, reputation matters in romance.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/j4vK4al.jpeg

In other words, even if rejected, one should not act desperate, but instead laugh it off gracefully. It’s important to maintain one’s dignity, as relationships between families may continue even after a rejection.

Erika, having understood my feelings during the carriage ride and showing me a roundabout noble attitude by allowing me to stay by her side for a year without responding to my affections, was still talking to me because she was a noble, regardless of her current status. She likely didn’t think I was still obsessively clinging to her.
Noble romances tend to end rather quickly.
I fumbled for words, hesitating. Was there a way to convey that if she wanted, I would overcome any obstacle to kill her enemies and charge into a horde of monsters for the down payment?
...Impossible? Yes, it was impossible. No matter how I put it, it would come off as too desperate.
"Are you really that averse to swinging your sword to earn money?"
As I struggled to find the right words, I was surprised to see Erika's face filled with unexpected concern.
I hurriedly opened my mouth.
"No, it’s not that. I was just thinking about how there might be people trying to interfere with whatever we do, considering your situation."
That wasn’t a lie, but it sounded like an excuse. For a moment, I thought it might be better to be completely honest, but no, if she thought I was being too desperate, I would die.
Erika seemed relieved by my excuse.
"I understand your concern regarding my situation."
But──, Erika straightened her back.
"That doesn’t mean I should be hindered. It would be quite vexing to take a detour just because there are those who would obstruct my path."
Her earlier anxious expression was replaced by a serious one.

"The path we walk is neither a path of conquest nor a royal road. It is the common path. A path that is found everywhere. To work, earn our daily bread, and seek a home to return to. It is a natural course of action for any human. Why should we be deterred from walking this common path? If there are those who obstruct it, we simply need to clear them away."
As expected, the daughter of the Solnzali family, known for their fiery temperament.
The way she described the common path was a bit too violent. However, it filled me with a sense of joy.

I had long since abandoned the noble's common path, yet here I was, walking alongside her on the path she claimed was common. Together, we would crush any obstacles in our way and pave a road laid with golden magic.
It was a position far beyond what a timid, ordinary person like me could hope for.
A smile crept onto my face at that stroke of luck.
"It sounds like an exciting common path."
Erika looked at me in surprise.
"I understand, Erika. Let’s go, down that common path."

I didn’t know how far I could accompany her, but until the day she tells me she doesn’t need me, I will walk alongside her. Whether she sensed my feelings or something else entirely, Erika returned my smile with a truly challenging grin.
Erika Solnzali was angry.
She was angry not only at her father for failing to handle the important matter of paying for their house but also at herself.
Being told she might lose her home, she was furious at herself for not having an immediate solution. She couldn’t believe she had stood idle in the face of such injustice, even for a moment.
Perhaps I am unexpectedly incompetent.
Since being exiled, she had come to strongly realize just how little she could do. Erika recognized that she had been relying on her status as a noble for far too long.
Being free, while it may seem obvious, meant taking responsibility for oneself.
And now, she was free as well.
Erika decided to change her mindset; she would discard the complacency she had grown accustomed to.
Thus, Erika intended to do what she could immediately.
In other words, she would hunt monsters to earn money.
In the process, raising Shin's adventurer rank would be killing two birds with one stone.
Erika was also displeased that Shin, who was being dragged into this farce for her sake, had such a low opinion of himself.
While he didn’t seem particularly interested in such things, she wished he would show at least a little interest. After all, he was a symbol of something special to her.
Well, that was just how he was, and it was fine.
So, when Erika saw Shin struggling with her proposal, she couldn’t help but feel anxious.

Was she forcing him to want something he didn’t desire for the down payment on "their" house? Was she imposing unreasonable expectations on him, forcing him into a situation where he had to sacrifice his freedom?
Was it really that unpleasant for him? She felt a wave of anxiety wash over her, but when she saw Shin shake his head, reassuring her that it wasn’t the case, she felt relieved.
He was simply considering her situation.
That made her happy.
Thus, Erika straightened her back.
She could simply clear away anyone who tried to obstruct her path. Shin had his own goals. She had enough strength to fend off any sparks that might fly in their direction.

Even if it meant sacrificing her own life, she wouldn’t give up on her desire to gain a connection with the Light Priestess, despite the difficulties of her lower noble status. Even with such thoughts, she found joy in the farce of being called his wife.
Let’s go together, down that common path.
As she responded to Shin, Erika smiled back.
As she responded to Shin, it was as if she was declaring that she would accompany him.
Hearing Erika’s declaration that she wouldn’t let go of her truly cool house made me ponder what to do.

It made sense that Erika was attached to that house, considering she was a noble. It was essentially a matter of face. For Erika, the daughter of a high noble, being kicked out of her house for failing to pay its price was likely unacceptable.

Unlike me, who would lose all reason to live with Erika if that house were gone, she had a different perspective. Honestly, if Erika were to say she wanted to live together, I would desperately scramble to find a way to gather the money.
But, a big game, huh? As I pondered, a voice I had coincidentally heard for the past two days suddenly reached my ears.
"I finally found you! The Longdagger couple!"
Yes, it’s the Longdagger couple, I thought, suppressing a sickly smile as I turned around to see Sister Shara from the church burst through the diner’s door, making a ruckus.

"I’m going to earn the down payment!" My previously buoyant mood deflated in an instant. Here came the obstacle to our common path. Had she been running? Shara approached our table, her face slightly flushed.
"What was that donation all about!?"
As soon as she reached us, Shara shouted.
"Was it too little after all?"
Erika replied calmly to the suddenly appearing sister, who had begun to complain. In fact, her tone even held a hint of apology.
Both Shara and I were taken aback.
"N-no, that’s not—"

Erika's expression conveyed her seriousness. Realizing this, Shara stumbled over her words. Meanwhile, I was moved by the fact that Erika, who had just been talking about needing money, showed no regret for the large donation she had made. That was so typical of Erika.
"No, it’s not that! I’m saying it’s too much!"
Shara slammed her hands on the table and, seemingly exasperated, threw her head back to the ceiling. What a noisy person.
"Why does it seem like I’m the one who’s angry!?"

Being asked that left me at a loss. Still, she might actually be quite an interesting person. Well, she had been on the verge of death when we first met, so any change in her impression could make her seem more interesting.
"If it’s too much, then that’s good."
"That’s not good!?"
What is she saying? Shara yelled.
"What do you think I felt when I went to the orphanage!? Even as a sister, everyone around me looked like a thief!?"
That’s a traumatic experience.
"You need to have the mindset to handle donations to the orphanage, don’t you think?"
In response, Erika nodded as if she found it insightful, which made me feel a bit sorry for Shara.
It was amusing to watch, though.
"This conversation isn’t getting through!"
"How rude, it is getting through."
Erika responded with a frown to Shara's words.
"Why should I be blamed for being 'too much'? If I were being blamed for being too little, that would be one thing, but what does 'too much' even mean?"

As someone who was currently struggling to figure out how to earn a down payment for a house, I was almost moved by Erika’s ability to respond with such indifference to being accused of giving too much. She was someone who had no regrets about her actions.
"The feelings of the person delivering it! Let’s think about that!"
Shara, unaware of the circumstances, was making a very valid point.
"That’s why, even though you’re a sister, you went to the orphanage with the mindset that everyone in the town was a thief, right? My choice of people was not wrong at all."
Shara looked up at the ceiling again, shouting, and while it was incorrect, it was somewhat gratifying!
I understood her feelings, but could she please quiet down a bit?
As I sipped my water, I thought about that.
I figured it was about time to settle down Shara, who seemed like she was about to get kicked out of the diner.

Since it was a diner catering to adventurers, they were probably used to some commotion and only frowned slightly. It wouldn’t have been surprising if they had kicked her out for making such a ruckus so early in the morning.
"So? What did you want with us? You wouldn’t be searching for us just because the donation amount was too high, would you?"

As I asked, I thought, no, she might actually do something like that. This sister had been trying to confront a Golden Ogre to save the villagers, even in a state where her bones were protruding from her abdomen.
She wasn’t the type to be quiet, and she was definitely not sane.
"Well, that’s part of it, but..."
Shara wet her lips with a sip of water.
"Given the amount, I thought I should report to the bishop after delivering it to the orphanage, so I did, and..."
For some reason, Shara wore a troubled smile.
"I was told to work under you two."
She looked at us as if asking, "What do you think?"
I grimaced deeply at Shara's words.
To summarize Shara's story:

After reporting the donation to the orphanage to the bishop, she had to explain that the adventurer couple who had saved her was us. Upon learning this, the bishop was quite impressed and instructed her to assist us, the adventurer couple who had done him a favor.
What a troublesome situation.

From Shara's perspective, we must have appeared to be the perfect adventurers who accepted a little girl’s request for free, defeated the Golden Ogre that was about to attack the village, and donated most of the money from selling its magic stone to the orphanage—exactly the kind of adventurers the church would favor.
If the church started to take a liking to us, we could expect requests for commissioned work, which was what I feared.
As a result, I never expected that a sister would be sent our way.
